text:
There's no single best combo for every RV, so here are picks by how you camp. The links go to the review pages that list each unit, and you can check current prices from there. I couldn't open retailer pages, so confirm prices and specs before you buy.

## Pick by your RV use

**Weekends, no air conditioning (fridge, lights, laptop, Starlink): about 1,000Wh**
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** is the best overall in [this camping comparison](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/). It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output, and up to 1,000W of solar input across two inputs. It's about 28 lb and expands to 5kWh. To use the full solar input, you need panels on both inputs.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is the simpler, lighter option at 1,070Wh and 23.8 lb ([same guide](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)). Solar input caps at 400W, so two 200W SolarSaga panels are the most it can use. It also can't take an add-on battery.

**Longer trips: about 2,000Wh**
- **BLUETTI AC200L** has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, and 1,200W of solar input, and the [EmergencyEnergy roundup](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) lists a built-in 30A RV port. It's heavy at about 62 lb.
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** has 2,042Wh and is lighter at about 39.5 lb, but its solar input is only 400W ([guide](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).

**Full-time or boondocking with a roof AC**
- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge, and expands past 12kWh. It's the top pick in the [EmergencyEnergy comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). That site estimates a 13,500 BTU AC (about 1,500W) runs roughly 2.3 hours on one battery. It's heavy, a two-person lift.
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** (3,024Wh, 3,000W) is the simpler option for running AC, per the same article.

## Deal I found
The **ALLPOWERS R4000** (3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, 2,000W solar input, 5-year warranty) is listed at $1,499. Code EXTRA12 brings it to $1,319.12 and expires 2026-11-15. The ALLPOWERS26 code (10% off) gives $1,349.10 and runs through 2026-12-30. The codes were tested in the store's cart on Oct 23–24, but the checkout has the final word. [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) (affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you; [details](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)). It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's best left in place, and each solar input maxes at 650W.

## Choosing panels
- Match panel wattage to the station's solar input limit. A big array into a 400W-limited unit is wasted.
- Folding panels like the Renogy 200W suitcase are a common pairing ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)). If you have roof space, a fixed array is better for a larger system.
- Solar panels are usually sold separately from the base unit, so check what a bundle includes.

## My recommendation
- **Most RVers:** the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus with two folding panels.
- **Running AC off-grid:** the DELTA Pro 3.
- **Tighter budget:** the BLUETTI AC200L or the ALLPOWERS deal.

If you tell me your RV type, whether you need AC, and your budget, I can narrow it to one.
